newsitem.title: INDIA: Charred India crash victims lie on ice in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Charred India crash victims lie on ice in hospital.

text.p: Three dozen bodies charred beyond recognition, victims of the world's worst mid-air crash, lie on melting ice slabs in an open Indian hospital courtyard.
Blood from the bodies mingles with water from melting ice as distraught relatives descend on the single-storey hospital.
The macabre scene on Thursday highlighted problems faced by Indian authorities after Tuesday's collision between a Saudi Arabian jumbo jet and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76.
The two aircraft carried a total of 349 people, according to official figures. All were killed.
Other bodies, not totally disfigured, were in rooms in the district hospital at Charkhi Dadri, in a rural area about 80 km (50 miles) west of New Delhi, India's capital.
They, too, had been placed on melting ice slabs in the hospital, which has only basic medical equipment.
Some corpses had been there for more than 24 hours following Tuesday evening's collision.
Officials said 257 bodies from the Saudi plane had been identified, as had all of 37, mainly Kazaks, from the Il-76.
Outside the hospital building, horse-drawn carriages with plain wooden coffins were drawn up.
Religious groups, including Hindus and Moslems, set up makeshift meeting places under canopies as they prepared to decide whether to bury or cremate unidentifiable corpses.
"We are hopeful of identifying more bodies," Mohammad Akil, a senior police superintendent, told Reuters.
"We will hold a meeting (with community religious leaders) this afternoon and decide whether to cremate or bury. By this evening or tomorrow morning, we will dispose of the bodies."
Up to 59 bodies were reported to have been handed over to relatives by late on Thursday.
Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim said on Wednesday 200 wooden coffins had been hastily prepared for victims' remains.
Authorities have arranged to embalm bodies destined for far-off places.
"In the crash, many were Moslems," Alimmuddin Asadi, a representative of the Moslem Jamiat Ulema Hind religious organisation, said.
"We want their last rites to be done according to Islamic ways. In Delhi, also, we have made arrangements for the burial of Moslem crash victims," he added.

Jet Ram Gupta, district head of the Hindu Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, said: "Those bodies not identifiable will be left to the district administration to decide on how to perform their last rites. We will not create any disputes.
